questions.statement: Report the sentence in indirect speech: She said, 'I am tired.'
questions.context: Transformacion de directo a indirecto, San Salvador.

options.text: She said that she is tired.
options.feedback: In reported speech the present simple becomes the past simple.

options.text: She said that she was tired.
options.feedback: Pronoun and tense shift: 'I' becomes 'she' and 'am' becomes 'was'.

options.text: She says that she was tired.
options.feedback: The reporting verb must be 'said' in the past to match the narrative tense.

options.text: She said that I was tired.
options.feedback: The pronoun refers to the reporter's 'I', which is wrong here.

questions.explanation:
Al pasar a indirecto, el pronombre 'I' se cambia a 'she' y el verbo 'am' pasa a 'was': los tiempos retroceden una unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct reported question: He asked me, 'Where do you live?'
questions.context: Preguntas en discurso indirecto, San Miguel.

options.text: He asked me where did I live.
options.feedback: Question word order cannot remain in a reported question.

options.text: He asked me where do I live.
options.feedback: 'Do' stays in the present only if the reporting verb is present, which it is not.

options.text: He asked me if where I lived.
options.feedback: 'If' introduces yes/no questions, not questions with a wh-word.

options.text: He asked me where I lived.
options.feedback: Direct questions become word-order statements with a backshifted verb.

questions.explanation:
En una pregunta indirecta se usa el orden de afirmativo: el auxiliar no se invierte con el sujeto.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Report this sentence: They said, 'We have finished the project.'
questions.context: Indirecto con presente perfecto, San Salvador.

options.text: They said that they have finished the project.
options.feedback: The tense has not been backshifted to the reporting past.

options.text: They said that we had finished the project.
options.feedback: The pronoun must refer to the same participants, so 'they' is correct.

options.text: They said that they had finished the project.
options.feedback: Present perfect backshifts to the past perfect 'had finished'.

options.text: They said that they would finish the project.
options.feedback: That would be a future in the past, not a backshift of the present perfect.

questions.explanation:
El presente perfecto 'have finished' retrocede a 'had finished' y el pronombre 'we' se conserva porque el sujeto es el mismo grupo.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which backshift is correct? He said, 'I will call you tomorrow.'
questions.context: Will por would en indirecto, San Salvador.

options.text: He said that he would call me the next day.
options.feedback: 'Will' becomes 'would'; 'the next day' is the classic time backshift.

options.text: He said that he will call me tomorrow.
options.feedback: Neither the modal nor the time expression has been backshifted.

options.text: He said that he calls me the next day.
options.feedback: The reporting tense is past, so the verb must be backshifted too.

options.text: He said that he would have called me the next day.
options.feedback: The past perfect would imply an action completed before another past moment.

questions.explanation:
'Will' se convierte en 'would' al pasar al discurso indirecto, y 'tomorrow' suele transformarse en 'the next day'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct reported statement: The teacher said, 'You must submit the report today.'
questions.context: Normas y obligaciones en indirecto, San Miguel.

options.text: The teacher said that we must submit the report today.
options.feedback: Leaving the modal and the time expression unchanged misses the tense shift.

options.text: The teacher said that we must to submit the report that day.
options.feedback: A modal can never be followed by 'to' in this structure.

options.text: The teacher said that we should submit the report that day.
options.feedback: 'Should' reports advice, not the obligation that was announced.

options.text: The teacher said that we had to submit the report that day.
options.feedback: 'Must' is reported as 'had to' when the obligation came from an external rule.

questions.explanation:
Las obligaciones externas ('must') se reportan como 'had to', y el tiempo 'today' pasa a 'that day'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Look at the sentence: 'She said that she is at home now.' What is wrong?
questions.context: Analisis de errores en indirecto, San Salvador.

options.text: Nothing is wrong; reported speech can keep the present tense.
options.feedback: The present can remain only in simultaneous-reporting cases, not in this narrative.

options.text: Only the pronoun 'she' is wrong.
options.feedback: The pronoun is correct because it refers to the subject of the reporting verb.

options.text: The verb should be 'was' and 'now' should become 'then'.
options.feedback: Both the tense backshift and the time expression must change in reported speech.

options.text: Only 'now' is wrong.
options.feedback: Both elements require modification; the verb backshift is mandatory.

questions.explanation:
El problema es doble: el verbo no retrocede a pasado y 'now' debe convertirse en 'then' cuando el contexto ya es pasado.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Report this sentence: The mechanic said, 'I can fix it tomorrow.'
questions.context: Discurso indirecto con verbos modales, San Salvador.

options.text: The mechanic said that he can fix it tomorrow.
options.feedback: Neither the modal nor the time expression has been backshifted to the reporting past.

options.text: The mechanic says that he could fix it the next day.
options.feedback: The reporting verb must remain in the past for the backshift to make sense.

options.text: The mechanic said that he must fix it the next day.
options.feedback: 'Must' would change the meaning from possibility to obligation.

options.text: The mechanic said that he could fix it the next day.
options.feedback: 'Can' becomes 'could' and 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day' in the reported clause.

questions.explanation:
El modal 'can' conserva su significado de posibilidad en el discurso indirecto, porque no tiene forma de pasado; solo cambia el modo de la oracion.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct report of a yes/no question. She asked me: 'Did you finish the homework?'
questions.context: Preguntas de si o no en indirecto, San Salvador.

options.text: She asked me if did I finish the homework.
options.feedback: The auxiliary must not be inverted in a reported question.

options.text: She asked me if I had finished the homework.
options.feedback: 'If' plus backshifted past perfect: standard reported yes/no question.

options.text: She asked me that I had finished the homework.
options.feedback: 'That' introduces statements, not questions.

options.text: She asked me if I finished the homework.
options.feedback: 'Finished' would be correct only with a present reporting verb.

questions.explanation:
Las preguntas de si o no se convierten con 'if' y el verbo se coloca antes del sujeto, en orden afirmativo.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct reported sentence: The doctor said, 'You should rest for a week.'
questions.context: Consejo medico en indirecto, San Miguel.

options.text: The doctor said that I should rest for a week.
options.feedback: 'Should' has no past form and remains unchanged in reported speech.

options.text: The doctor said that I should rest for a week ago.
options.feedback: 'A week ago' would place the rest in the past, which contradicts the advice.

options.text: The doctor said that I rested for a week.
options.feedback: Dropping the modal loses the advisory meaning of the original sentence.

options.text: The doctor said that I would rest for a week.
options.feedback: 'Would' would report a future event, not advice given in the past.

questions.explanation:
El consejo con 'should' se reporta con 'should' mas verbo base, porque 'should' no tiene forma de pasado.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What happens to the possessive in this report? She said, 'This is my book.'
questions.context: Pronombres posesivos en indirecto, San Salvador.

options.text: It becomes 'her book' to keep the reference to the same person.
options.feedback: Reporting requires the possessive to shift so ownership stays the same.

options.text: It becomes 'my book' because the speaker takes ownership.
options.feedback: That would change the meaning: the book belongs to the woman, not to the reporter.

options.text: It becomes 'their book'.
options.feedback: The pronoun 'their' has no basis in the original sentence.

options.text: The possessive disappears and only 'the book' remains.
options.feedback: Removing the possessive loses the ownership information entirely.

questions.explanation:
Los posesivos cambian para mantener el referente: 'my' se convierte en 'her' porque el Dueño es la mujer que hablo.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Report this question: He asked, 'What time does the meeting start?'
questions.context: Preguntas indirectas con wh-questions, San Salvador.

options.text: He asked what time did the meeting start.
options.feedback: Inverted question order cannot survive into the reported clause.

options.text: He asked what time the meeting will start.
options.feedback: The tense must move to the past because the reporting verb is past.

options.text: He asked what time the meeting started.
options.feedback: Wh-word retained, auxiliary before the subject, tense backshifted.

options.text: He asked that what time the meeting started.
options.feedback: 'That' cannot introduce a wh-question directly.

questions.explanation:
La wh-word se conserva, el auxiliar retrocede y el orden se vuelve afirmativo: 'what time the meeting started'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.context: Evaluacion de discurso indirecto, San Salvador.

options.text: The manager told us that we will be notified by email.
options.feedback: No backshift was applied even though the reporting verb is past.

options.text: The manager told us that we will notified by email.
options.feedback: Two errors: the passive is missing and the tense was not backshifted.

options.text: The manager told that we would be notified by email.
options.feedback: The reported clause needs the subject 'we' explicitly retained.

options.text: The manager told us that we would be notified by email.
options.feedback: 'Would be notified' correctly reports a future passive event.

questions.explanation:
El discurso indirecto exige un verbo de reporte en pasado y un retroceso consistente de los tiempos verbales.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What does 'He told me that he had been waiting for an hour' tell us?
questions.context: Comprension del discurso indirecto, San Salvador.

options.text: He waited for an hour and will wait more.
options.feedback: The sentence makes no claim about a future action.

options.text: He had already been waiting for an hour at that past moment.
options.feedback: Past perfect continuous shows the waiting started earlier and was still ongoing.

options.text: He is waiting for an hour now.
options.feedback: Present continuous is not what 'had been waiting' expresses.

options.text: He had waited for an hour before he started.
options.feedback: The continuous form stresses the ongoing activity, not a completed one.

questions.explanation:
'Had been waiting' es un pasado perfecto progresivo: la espera comenzo antes y se extendia hasta ese momento pasado.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct reporting verb. 'Stop talking!', she said to me.
questions.context: Seleccion del verbo de reporte, San Salvador.

options.text: told
options.feedback: 'Told' plus object plus reported command is the correct pattern here.

options.text: suggested
options.feedback: 'Suggested' would require a proposal of options rather than a command.

options.text: warned
options.feedback: 'Warned' would imply the speaker anticipated a negative consequence.

options.text: ordered
options.feedback: 'Ordered' usually requires an authority, such as the police or a judge.

questions.explanation:
'Told' se usa para transmision de ordenes o mensajes; 'said' funciona con citas directas.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct report of a command: He said to us, 'Wait here!'
questions.context: Ordenes en discurso indirecto, San Salvador.

options.text: He told us waiting there.
options.feedback: A gerund cannot replace the to-infinitive after 'told somebody to do'.

options.text: He told us to wait there.
options.feedback: 'Told' plus object plus to-infinitive is the standard pattern for reporting commands.

options.text: He told us that we must wait there.
options.feedback: A that-clause with a modal is possible but less direct than the infinitive pattern.

options.text: He told we to wait there.
options.feedback: 'Told' requires an object pronoun: 'told us', not 'told we'.

questions.explanation:
El imperativo se reporta con 'told us to wait', usando el infinitivo despues de 'to'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct question in reported speech: 'Where are you going?' he asked.
questions.context: Preguntas indirectas con el verbo be, San Salvador.

options.text: He asked where are I going.
options.feedback: Auxiliary inversion is not allowed in a reported question.

options.text: He asked where I am going.
options.feedback: No tense backshift was applied, although the reporting verb is 'asked'.

options.text: He asked where I was going.
options.feedback: Present 'are' becomes past 'was' in the reported question.

options.text: He asked where I were going.
options.feedback: 'Were' does not agree with the first person singular 'I'; it would be 'was'.

questions.explanation:
El verbo 'be' en presente se convierte en 'was' en el pasado simple dentro del discurso indirecto.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence contains a report of the past perfect?
questions.context: Identificacion del pasado perfecto en indirecto, San Miguel.

options.text: She said that she is going home.
options.feedback: Present continuous is not a past perfect form.

options.text: She said that she had already gone home.
options.feedback: 'Had gone' places the departure before another past moment.

options.text: She said that she would go home.
options.feedback: That is a future in the past, not a past perfect.

options.text: She said that she goes home.
options.feedback: Present simple would need a present reporting verb.

questions.explanation:
'Had gone' es pasado perfecto: una accion pasada anterior a otra referencia temporal pasada.

questions.statement: Complete the text: 'The guide told the tourists that the museum ____ closed on Mondays.'
questions.context: Informacion reportada sobre horarios, San Salvador.

options.text: was
options.feedback: 'Is closed' backshifts to 'was closed' inside the reported clause.

options.text: is
options.feedback: No tense backshift was applied to the reported clause.

options.text: will be
options.feedback: 'Will be' would report a future fact, not the museum's regular closing day.

options.text: has been
options.feedback: 'Has been' would suggest the museum has remained closed since that Monday.

questions.explanation:
El verbo 'is closed' en presente se reporta como 'was closed' en pasado simple. El tiempo verbal del enunciado se conserva al reportarlo.

questions.statement: What is the main difference between direct and reported speech?
questions.context: Consolidacion del tema, San Salvador.

options.text: Only the pronouns change.
options.feedback: Tenses and question forms also change; pronouns are only part of the process.

options.text: Nothing changes except the punctuation.
options.feedback: Ignoring all these changes would leave the two forms identical.

options.text: The meaning always disappears in reported speech.
options.feedback: Reported speech preserves the meaning while changing the grammatical form.

options.text: Tenses, pronouns, questions and time expressions change.
options.feedback: Reported speech reformulates the same information from another point in time.

questions.explanation:
En el discurso indirecto el contenido se conserva, pero cambian los tiempos verbales, los pronombres, las preguntas y las expresiones de tiempo.

questions.statement: Choose the best correction of this sentence: 'He said that he is very tired.'
questions.context: Correccion de concordancia temporal, San Miguel.

options.text: He said that he very tired.
options.feedback: Removing the verb entirely leaves an incomplete clause.

options.text: He says that he is very tired.
options.feedback: Changing the reporting verb to the present is a rewrite, not a correction of the backshift.

options.text: He said that he was very tired.
options.feedback: The present simple in the reported clause must become the past simple.

options.text: He said that he has been very tired.
options.feedback: 'Has been' implies a duration up to now, which the original does not express.

questions.explanation:
Cuando el verbo de reporte esta en pasado ('said'), el contenido tambien retrocede: 'is' pasa a 'was'.
